glosses.notes: 夸奖 means to praise someone for doing something well.

examples.sentence: 老师先没有夸奖那个孩子，而是让他把前面怎么想到的慢慢说出来，因为大家都想跟着学。
母亲平时很少夸奖人，所以那天她一开口夸奖那个孩子，大家就知道他这次做得很好。
经理说可以夸奖年轻人，可是夸奖的时候最好把哪一点做得好说明白，这样后面他们才知道怎么继续。

example_translations.translation: The teacher did not praise that child right away, but first asked him to slowly explain how he had thought of it earlier, because everyone wanted to learn from him.
Mother rarely praises people, so the moment she began praising that child that day, everyone knew he had done very well this time.
The manager said young people can certainly be praised, but when praising them it is best to explain clearly what they did well, so later they know how to continue.

glosses.notes: 夸张 describes something stretched beyond what is realistic or natural.

examples.sentence: 他把事情说得太夸张了，所以刚开始大家都吓了一跳，后来才发现真正的问题没有那么大。
老师说写文章可以更有意思一点，可是如果每一句都很夸张，读的人反而不知道哪一部分最重要。
那张海报颜色很亮，字也很大，看上去有一点夸张，可是站远一点以后反而特别清楚。

example_translations.translation: He described the matter in such an exaggerated way that everyone was startled at first, but later they realized the real problem was not that big.
The teacher said writing can be made more interesting, but if every sentence is exaggerated, readers instead do not know which part matters most.
The poster had very bright colors and very large words, so it looked a bit exaggerated, but from farther away it actually became especially clear.

glosses.notes: 会计 is an accountant, the person who handles and records financial accounts.

examples.sentence: 公司新来的会计做事很仔细，所以前面积下来的几个小问题，她一看就知道该从哪里查起。
父亲年轻的时候做过会计，因此到现在看见别人把数字写错，还是会马上忍不住提醒一句。
经理说会计不是只会算钱，还要把每一笔进出的钱都写清楚，不然后面谁都看不明白。

example_translations.translation: The company’s new accountant works very carefully, so as soon as she looked at the small problems that had built up earlier, she knew where to begin checking.
Father worked as an accountant when he was young, so even now, when he sees someone write a number incorrectly, he still cannot help giving an immediate reminder.
The manager said an accountant does not only know how to calculate money, but also has to write each sum coming in and going out clearly, or later no one will understand the accounts.

glosses.notes: 快捷 means quick and convenient, especially in a practical or efficient way.

examples.sentence: 这条路虽然不是最近的，可是地铁一通以后比原来快捷得多，所以很多人现在上班都改从这里走。
老师说用工具当然快捷，可是如果你一点原理都不懂，后面一出小问题就还是得停下来。
他把常用的地方都放在前面，所以后面要找的时候会快捷很多，也不用一个一个看。

example_translations.translation: Although this route is not the shortest, once the subway opened it became much quicker than before, so many people now go this way to work.
The teacher said using tools is certainly quick, but if you do not understand the principles at all, you still have to stop once a small problem appears later.
He put the places he uses most often at the front, so later when he needs to find something it is much quicker and he does not have to look through them one by one.

glosses.notes: 款 can mean a sum of money, and it can also count different versions or models of an item.

examples.sentence: 经理说那笔款今天下午应该能到，所以前面已经答应好的东西，现在就可以先开始准备了。
这家店今年新出了三款衣服，母亲看了很久，最后还是觉得最简单的那一款更好看。
父亲把收到的款都写得很清楚，因为前面少写一点，后面的数字就容易全乱。

example_translations.translation: The manager said that sum of money should arrive this afternoon, so the things already promised earlier can now begin to be prepared first.
This shop released three new styles of clothes this year, and after looking for a long time, Mother still felt that the simplest one looked best.
Father writes down every sum of money received very clearly, because if even a little is omitted earlier, the numbers later easily become completely confused.

glosses.notes: 款式 means the style or design of clothes, products, or other objects.

examples.sentence: 这件衣服的款式很简单，可是颜色和布都很舒服，所以母亲一试就觉得平时上班也能穿。
这家店的人说最近很多人喜欢这种款式，因为看上去简单，所以平时穿也很方便。
设计的人把旧照片看了很久，才决定把前面的款式稍微改一点，让现在的人看着也不会觉得太老。

example_translations.translation: The style of this piece of clothing is very simple, but the color and fabric are both comfortable, so as soon as Mother tried it on, she felt she could wear it to work normally.
People at this shop said many customers have recently liked this style, because it looks simple and is also very convenient to wear in daily life.
The designer looked at old photos for a long time before deciding to change the earlier style a little, so people today would not feel it looked too old.

glosses.notes: 亏损 means to suffer a financial loss.

examples.sentence: 这家店前两个月一直在亏损，所以经理后来先把最不赚钱的那一部分停下来，想看后面会不会好一点。
父亲说做生意偶尔亏损并不可怕，可怕的是已经看见问题了，还是一直不肯改办法。
公司原来以为今年不会再亏损，可是市场一变，前面刚准备好的计划后面又得重新算。

example_translations.translation: This shop kept losing money in the last two months, so the manager later first stopped the part that earned the least, hoping to see whether things would improve afterward.
Father said that losing money occasionally in business is not frightening; what is frightening is seeing the problem already and still refusing to change the method.
The company originally thought it would not lose money again this year, but once the market changed, the plan prepared earlier had to be recalculated afterward.

glosses.notes: 困扰 means to trouble or bother someone over time.

examples.sentence: 这个问题已经困扰他很久了，所以老师这次没有马上给答案，而是先带他把前面想过的办法重新看一遍。
失眠一直困扰着那位老人，因此白天看起来很简单的小事，到了晚上反而会让他更容易紧张。
经理说真正困扰公司的不是钱太少，而是大家明明都很努力，却总是没有把力气放在一个地方。

example_translations.translation: This problem has troubled him for a long time, so this time the teacher did not give the answer immediately, but first went back through the methods he had thought about earlier.
Insomnia has continued to trouble that old man, so small things that seem simple in the daytime instead make him more nervous at night.
The manager said what truly troubles the company is not having too little money, but that although everyone works hard, they never put their effort in one place.

glosses.notes: 扩展 means to make something larger in range, scale, or content.

examples.sentence: 学校打算把图书室再往后面扩展一点，因为现在来的人越来越多，原来的地方一到下午就坐不下了。
老师说学一门语言不能只背单词，还要靠大量阅读慢慢扩展自己的理解，不然后面很难真正用起来。
公司把业务从城里扩展到周围几个地方以后，才发现原来那套管理办法已经不太够用了。

example_translations.translation: The school plans to expand the library room a bit farther back, because more and more people come now, and by the afternoon the original space cannot hold everyone.
The teacher said that learning a language cannot rely only on memorizing words; one must also expand one’s understanding gradually through extensive reading, or later it becomes hard to use it well.
After the company expanded its business from the city to several surrounding places, it discovered that the original management methods were no longer quite enough.

glosses.notes: 落 means to be left behind or fall behind others or the expected progress.

examples.sentence: 我前面两天没来，所以今天一看后面的内容，就知道自己已经落了不少，只能晚上回家慢慢看。
他跑到最后不是因为一开始不认真，而是中间鞋出了问题，一停下来以后就一下落在别人后面了。
老师提醒大家如果前面有地方没听明白，就要马上问，不然问题一多，后面很容易越落越远。

example_translations.translation: I was absent the previous two days, so as soon as I looked at the later material today, I knew I had already fallen behind quite a bit and could only go home and study slowly at night.
He ended up at the back not because he was careless at the start, but because there was a problem with his shoes in the middle, and once he stopped, he suddenly fell behind everyone else.

The teacher reminded everyone that if there is a part earlier they do not understand clearly, they should ask immediately, or once the problems pile up, it becomes easy to fall farther and farther behind.

glosses.notes: 辣椒 is a chili pepper used as food or seasoning.

examples.sentence: 这道菜里虽然放了辣椒，可是味道并不太重，所以平时不太能吃辣的人也可以慢慢试一点。
母亲切辣椒的时候总会先开窗，因为要是里面的空气不动，站在旁边的人就很容易不舒服。
老人年轻时在南方住过，所以后来不管做什么菜，总觉得少一点辣椒，味道就差了很多。

example_translations.translation: Although chili pepper was added to this dish, the flavor is not too strong, so even people who usually cannot eat very spicy food can try a little slowly.
Mother always opens the window first when cutting chili peppers, because if the air inside does not move, people standing nearby become uncomfortable very easily.
The old man lived in the south when he was young, so later no matter what dish he made, he always felt that with less chili pepper the taste became much worse.

glosses.notes: 啦 is a sentence-ending particle that adds emphasis, certainty, or a lively tone.

examples.sentence: 别着急啦，我们前面已经把最难的地方准备好了，现在只要一个一个做，后面不会乱的。
天快黑啦，母亲在门口叫孩子现在回家，因为要是再晚一点，后面走路就不方便了。
你放心啦，经理刚才已经把要改的地方都说得很清楚了，我们照着做就不会差太远。

example_translations.translation: Do not worry; we have already prepared the hardest parts earlier, and now as long as we do things one by one, it will not get messy later.
It is getting dark already, and Mother called from the doorway for the child to come home now, because if it gets any later, walking afterward will be inconvenient.
Do not worry; the manager has already explained the parts that need changing very clearly, and if we follow that, we will not go too far wrong.

glosses.notes: 来临 means to arrive or come upon a time, season, event, or change.

examples.sentence: 考试来临以前，老师没有让大家一味加快速度，而是先把最容易错的地方一个一个重新看清楚。
冬天真正来临的时候，这条河边的风会比城里大很多，所以老人总提醒孩子出门多穿一点。
变化来临之前，很多人其实已经感觉到不一样了，只是那时候谁也说不清后面会变成什么样。

example_translations.translation: Before the exam arrived, the teacher did not simply tell everyone to speed up, but first had them look again at the parts most likely to be wrong one by one.
When winter truly arrives, the wind by this river becomes much stronger than in the city, so the old man always reminds the child to wear a little more before going out.
Before change arrived, many people had already felt that things were different, but at that time no one could explain clearly what things would become later.

glosses.notes: 来往 means to have movement back and forth, or to keep regular contact with someone.

examples.sentence: 这条路虽然不大，可是每天早上来往的人很多，所以住在这里的人早就习惯了外面的声音。
两家原来一直有来往，后来因为工作都忙，见面的次数才慢慢少了下来，可是感情并没有变。
老师说和人来往的时候，不只是要会说话，也要知道什么时候该安静听别人把意思讲完。

example_translations.translation: Although this road is not large, many people come and go here every morning, so the people living here have long grown used to the sounds outside.
The two families used to keep in contact all the time, and later the number of meetings gradually decreased because work kept them busy, but the relationship did not change.
The teacher said that when dealing with people, one must not only know how to speak, but also know when to listen quietly until the other person finishes explaining their meaning.

glosses.notes: 赖 can describe something as poor in quality in some contexts, and it can also mean relying on something or someone.

examples.sentence: 这个小地方这些年能慢慢好起来，全赖大家一直肯帮忙，不然前面说过的很多计划都做不成。
老人说一家人过去一直赖这片地过日子，所以一到天不好，心里就会比平时更不安。
经理提醒年轻人不能什么都赖别人来做，因为要是真的想往前走，很多地方还是得自己学会。

example_translations.translation: This small place has gradually improved over the years entirely because everyone kept being willing to help; otherwise many of the plans mentioned earlier could not have been carried out.
The old man said the family had long depended on this piece of land to make a living, so whenever the weather turned bad, they felt more uneasy than usual.
The manager reminded the young people that they cannot rely on others to do everything, because if they truly want to move forward, they still have to learn many things themselves.

glosses.notes: 拦 means to stop, block, or hold someone back from going on.

examples.sentence: 门口那位老人一看见孩子要往马路中间跑，就马上伸手把他拦下来，连话都没来得及先说。
警察把大家先拦在外面，不是故意不让进，而是里面还有事情没有处理完，现在进去反而更危险。
她本来想直接走，可是朋友在后面一直把她拦住，要她先把心里想说的话讲出来。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the old man at the door saw the child about to run into the middle of the road, he immediately reached out and stopped him before he even had time to say anything first.
The police first kept everyone outside, not because they intentionally did not want anyone to enter, but because things inside had not been handled yet and going in now would be more dangerous.
She originally wanted to leave directly, but her friend kept stopping her from behind and wanted her to first say what she had been wanting to say.

glosses.notes: 栏 can mean a railing or divider, and it can also mean a column or section in print or on a page.

examples.sentence: 报纸最后一栏专门写普通人的小事，所以父亲每次看到那一页，都会比看前面的消息更认真。
桥边那一栏太低了，母亲怕孩子一高兴就往前爬，所以一直让他走在自己里面一点。
老师把学生常错的几个字专门放到黑板旁边那一栏里，想让大家每天进来都先看一眼。

example_translations.translation: The last column of the newspaper is specially for ordinary people’s small stories, so each time Father sees that page, he reads it more carefully than the earlier news.
That railing by the bridge is too low, and Mother worries the child will climb forward once he gets excited, so she keeps him walking a little farther inside by her side.
The teacher put the characters students often get wrong into that column beside the blackboard, wanting everyone to look at them first each day when they come in.

glosses.notes: 兰花 is an orchid, often associated with elegance and careful growing.

examples.sentence: 那盆兰花看着安静，可是要把它养好并不容易，所以老人每天早上都会先去看土和水是不是合适。
母亲原来以为兰花太难照顾，后来跟着会养花的人学了一段时间，才知道很多地方只要慢一点就行。
画里的兰花不大，可是线条很轻，一放到大片空白前面，就让人马上安静下来。

example_translations.translation: That pot of orchids looks calm and quiet, but raising it well is not easy, so every morning the old man first goes to check whether the soil and water are suitable.

Mother originally thought orchids were too hard to care for, but after learning for a while from someone who knows how to grow flowers, she realized many parts only require moving a little more slowly.
The orchids in the painting are not large, but the lines are very light, and once they are placed in front of a wide blank space, they immediately make a person feel calm.

glosses.notes: 烂 means rotten, damaged, or worn so badly that it is no longer good.

examples.sentence: 那个苹果已经有一点烂了，所以母亲马上把它拿走，怕放久了以后别的也跟着坏。
这双鞋虽然没有完全烂，可是已经旧得很厉害了，再穿下去就不太行了。
老人说那些年家里再难，也不会把烂东西拿给客人，因为人穷一点，心里也不能少那份认真。

example_translations.translation: That apple had already gone a little rotten, so Mother immediately took it away, worried that if it stayed there too long the others would spoil as well.
Although this pair of shoes is not completely worn out, it has already become very old, and if it keeps being worn, it really will not do much longer.

The old man said that no matter how difficult things were at home in those years, they would never give rotten or damaged things to guests, because even if people are poor, they should not lose that careful respect.

glosses.notes: 狼 is a wolf, the animal often used in stories and descriptions of the wild.

examples.sentence: 孩子第一次在书里读到狼的时候有一点怕，可是老师让他把后面的故事看完以后，他反而想得更多了。
山里的人说以前晚上偶尔会听见狼叫，所以天一黑，家里大人就会早点叫孩子回家。
他觉得狼画得不太好，所以又改了很久，想让那只狼看上去自然一点。

example_translations.translation: The first time the child read about a wolf in a book, he felt a little afraid, but after the teacher had him finish the story later, he actually started thinking more deeply.
People in the mountains say that in the past they would occasionally hear wolves howl at night, so once it got dark, the adults at home would call the children back early.
He felt the wolf had not been painted very well, so he kept revising it for a long time, wanting that wolf to look a little more natural.

glosses.notes: 朗读 means to read something aloud so that others can hear it clearly.

examples.sentence: 老师先让大家把那一段安静看一遍，然后才请一个学生站起来朗读，因为她想让每个人先有自己的理解。
他小时候不敢在很多人前面朗读，可是后面读得多了，也就没有原来那么怕了。
母亲说每天花一点时间朗读很有用，因为说出来以后，很多地方会记得更清楚。

example_translations.translation: The teacher first let everyone read that passage quietly once and only then asked one student to stand up and read it aloud, because she wanted each person to have their own understanding first.
When he was young, he did not dare read aloud in front of many people, but after doing it more later, he was no longer as afraid as before.
Mother said spending a little time each day reading aloud is very useful, because after saying things out loud, many parts are remembered more clearly.

glosses.notes: 牢 can mean a prison, and as an adjective it can describe something firmly fixed or secure.

examples.sentence: 这根东西系得很牢，所以外面的风虽然很大，门口那块布还是没有掉下来。
父亲把那个袋子系得很牢，因为里面的东西很重要，他怕走到半路掉下来。
故事里那个做坏事的人后来被关进牢里，可是老师让大家讨论的重点其实不是他有没有受罚。

example_translations.translation: This thing was tied very firmly, so although the wind outside was strong, the piece of cloth at the doorway still did not fall down.
Father tied that bag very firmly because what was inside was important, and he worried it might fall down halfway along the road.
In the story, the person who did bad things was later shut into prison, but the point the teacher asked everyone to discuss was not actually whether he had been punished.

glosses.notes: 劳动力 means the labor force, or the people available to do work.

examples.sentence: 这个地方年轻劳动力越来越少，所以很多原来靠人手慢慢做的事，现在都得想别的办法来完成。
经理说公司不是完全没有劳动力，而是会做那项工作的人太少，所以前面的计划一直推不快。
研究的人发现劳动力一变化，后面连房子、学校和车的安排都得跟着一起改。

example_translations.translation: There is less and less young labor force in this place, so many things that originally depended on people doing them by hand now need other methods to be completed.
The manager said the company does not entirely lack labor, but that too few people know how to do that task, so the earlier plan has never been able to move forward quickly.
Researchers found that once the labor force changes, later even arrangements for housing, schools, and transport must all change with it.

glosses.notes: 老实 means honest, straightforward, or well-behaved.

examples.sentence: 这个孩子平时看着很老实，可是一到关键的时候却总能自己想出办法，所以老师一直很喜欢他。
父亲说做人老实当然重要，可是老实不是让你什么都不说，而是心里怎么想就怎么讲清楚。
母亲看弟弟今天特别老实，就知道他多半已经知道自己前面做错了什么，所以没有马上批评。

example_translations.translation: This child usually seems very honest and well-behaved, but when crucial moments come, he can always think of a solution himself, so the teacher has always liked him very much.
Father said that being honest is certainly important, but honesty does not mean saying nothing; it means explaining clearly what you truly think.
Seeing that my younger brother was especially well-behaved today, Mother knew he had probably already understood what he had done wrong earlier, so she did not criticize him immediately.

glosses.notes: 老鼠 is a mouse or rat, especially the small animal that appears in houses or storage areas.

examples.sentence: 前两天这里突然有了老鼠，所以经理马上让人把旧东西都拿出去，怕后面越来越多。
孩子一看见那只小老鼠从桌子下面跑过去，就先吓得站到门边，可是后来又忍不住想再看一眼。
老人说以前家里一有老鼠，大家晚上就会把门关好，也会把东西放高一点。

example_translations.translation: Two days ago mice suddenly appeared here, so the manager immediately had people take all the old things out, worried there would be more and more later.
As soon as the child saw that little mouse run past under the table, he was so frightened that he stood by the door, but later he still could not resist wanting another look.
The old man said that whenever there were mice at home in the past, everyone would shut the doors well at night and also put things a little higher up.
